decisive_items: Several vesicles with an erythematous base were observed on the lower back and left thigh.
Hematoxylin-eosin stain showed focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis with numerous filamentous bacilli with septa
Gram stain revealed numerous gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis
response.rationale: Neutropenic fever with scattered erythematous vesicular skin lesions and Gram-stain-visible rods in necrotic tissue is most consistent with ecthyma gangrenosum; Pseudomonas aeruginosa is the likely causative organism, but the specific clinicopathologic diagnosis is ecthyma gangrenosum.

rejected.why: This is the probable microbial cause rather than the specific clinical-pathologic skin diagnosis supported by the vignette
Neutropenic fever is the systemic context but does not explain the characteristic necrotic vesicular skin lesions.
Classic cutaneous anthrax is not supported by this neutropenic catheter-associated presentation and the lesion morphology is better explained by ecthyma gangrenosum.
The necrosis is limited to epidermal and subepidermal tissue, without a pattern of deep fascial spread expected in necrotizing fasciitis.
